To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the serine proteases, HtrA2 and HtrA2-Omi, terminate cytomegalovirus infection.
the viral mitochondria-localised inhibitor of apoptosis (UL37x1; vMIA) blocks cell death in infected cells by inhibiting a serine protease (HtrA2) dependent pathway.
the CMV-encoded vMIA suppresses a caspase independent death pathway that is initiated by the serine-protease HtrA-2/Omi.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of programmed cell death.
the identification of a novel serine-dependent death pathway and the characterization of a viral inhibitor of the protease Htr2/Omi.
the molecular basis of cell death in CMV-infected cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vMIA is a multifunctional inhibitor of host cell death pathways that is required for the completion of CMV infection.
HtrA2 is a key player of the CMV-induced cell death pathway.
the vMIA suppresses the CMV infected cell death pathway by inhibiting the HtrA serine protease activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vMIA suppresses HtrA2-mediated cmvPCD and thereby prolongs virus production.
vMIA is a multifunctional inhibitor of apoptosis, autophagy and serine protease-mediated cell death.
CMV infection terminates by a novel serine-protease-dependent, caspase-independent programmed cell death pathway that is controlled by a mitochondria-localized viral inhibitor of apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the viral mitochondria-localization inhibitor of apoptosis (MIA) controls a caspase- and autophagy-independent cell death pathway that is triggered by the serine endopeptidase HtrA/Omi.
vMIA is a multifunctional protein that suppresses apoptosis, autophagy and serine protease dependent programmed cell death.
CMV has evolved to suppress multiple cell death pathways to ensure that the virus is able to produce a large number of virions.
